summary: A project can now set each tier's model and reasoning effort per host and move any role to another tier, through the new `/configure models` topic; `workspace/config.json` records only these overrides, and setup writes none of them. `tier_models` maps a host and one of the high, medium and low tiers to a `model`, an exact model ID of that host's model list or `session`, which runs the tier's roles on the session's model, and an `effort`; either key may be left out, and a missing key keeps the package value. `role_tiers` moves any role, the generated `-lens` and `-mechanical` variants included, to the high, medium or low tier on every host. A role's tier comes from `role_tiers`, else the package, and that tier's model and effort from `tier_models`, else the package's `auto` profile: the new `role_settings.py` is the one resolution that `project_config.py` and both host project generators use. An effort must be one the chosen model takes: a catalog model's catalog efforts, any effort the host's catalog knows for `session`, and the host's vocabulary for another model ID, which is checked only for its shape until the host's own model list is read. Codex `ultra` is refused for every tier, because a role at `ultra` starts subagents of its own, and `max` is written only with `--confirmed`, after a confirmation question that states the vendors' cost evidence recorded in `platforms/<host>/effort-policy.json`. `project_config.py set-tier --host --tier [--model] [--effort] [--confirmed] | --default` and `set-role-tier --role --tier | --default` write the overrides and record nothing equal to the package value, so a later package change reaches the project; `--default` removes an override the config holds even for a tier, host or role the package no longer has. Like `set`, both verbs refuse a missing config and one whose fields, schema, team or languages `check` refuses, and they add no override error, while one the config already had may stay. `project_config.py tiers` prints the config-level effective map, labelled so because model availability is the generators' to judge, and with `--model-list` each tier's model choices: the package model first, then the models of the active host's own model list that its picker shows, through its `host_models` adapter when the package ships one, else the package catalog, then `session`, each with its efforts and its recommended effort. `/configure models` asks per tier for the model first, then the effort, each laid out within the per-question option bound each host contract states, two to four options for Claude Code's `AskUserQuestion` and two to three for Codex's `request_user_input`, a `More choices` option opening the next question with the rest and `max` coming last with its confirmation; it then asks which roles move tier, writes through these verbs, renders the roles again and presents the effective table. The plugin's vault hook keeps a `set-tier` or `set-role-tier` write under an exact option parse, `--config` naming the project's config, and still restores any other Bash change to `workspace/config.json`. Setup keeps both overrides, dropping only empty maps, and stops on one the installed package no longer takes, naming the tier or role. Every build ships `templates/tier-map.json` with each role's tier and, per host, each tier's model, effort and the efforts its model takes, the host's model catalog, its effort vocabulary and the shape of a model ID of its list. On Claude Code, setup and refresh render every role, the variants included, into `.claude/agents/software-engineering-team-<role>.md` with its resolved `model`, `session` as `model: inherit`, and `effort`, remove rendered files the package no longer ships and refuse a user file that takes a rendered name; they own and remove only the top-level `software-engineering-team-*.md` files that carry the generated header, and list any other file with that header, such as a user's copy of a rendered role, under `kept` and leave it; the first render needs a Claude Code restart, which setup reports. The Claude Code host contract spawns `software-engineering-team-<role>` when the session lists it and otherwise the plugin's `software-engineering-team:<role>`, telling the user once why the project's model settings are not in effect. Each rendered file's header stamps the package version, the sha256 of its source agent and the sha256 of its resolved model and effort. At session start `team_guard.py register` reports rendered files whose stamp does not match the installed package or the project's `workspace/config.json`, as after a plugin update, or a config change such as a pull, before setup runs: it tells the user once per session to run setup or a package refresh and tells Claude, through its context, to spawn the plugin's `software-engineering-team:<role>` for every role until then, as the host contract's spawn rule does. Claude Code's model fallback hook treats `software-engineering-team-<role>` as the same role and takes its pin from that rendered file, or from the tier map when the project holds none, and stays silent without a pin, as for `session`. The generated `CLAUDE.md` now says to use this team's agents rather than its namespaced ones. On Codex, setup and refresh render each role's resolved `model`, none for `session`, and `model_reasoning_effort` into its role file, keep the effort under the `inherit` profile and a model fallback alike, including a run-time fallback that `--inherit-model` records until `--restore-model` or `--execution-profile auto`, and judge against this host's own model list, and accept for `--inherit-model`, the models the project resolves. The last header line of each Codex role file carries the same stamp, and the Codex package's `team_guard.py register` reports a role file whose stamp does not match and tells the user once per session to run setup, since Codex has no other identity of a role to start instead; a pulled `tier_models` or `role_tiers` change therefore no longer leaves `.codex/agents/` on the old model and effort without a word. Both project generators report the `roles` table, each role's tier, model and effort with their sources, beside the `tier_map` they rendered, and a `notice` that says whether a running session picks up what they wrote. Generated role files are never edited by hand. `tools/validate.py` checks each host's effort policy (`effort_policy`).
